points.what: EMEA orders rose 20.0% WoW and were the largest contributor to total order growth this week.
points.so_what: EMEA's growth was the main reason total orders grew despite declines elsewhere.

points.what: APAC orders fell 9.4% WoW, the biggest drag on total order growth.
points.so_what: APAC's pullback nearly offset the gains from other regions, muting the week's overall order growth.

points.what: Organic orders grew 23.4% WoW, the top contributor among traffic sources to order growth.
points.so_what: Organic's gain helped offset a 2.7% WoW decline in Search, the largest traffic source.

points.what: AOV was $85.64, up 0.8% WoW but down 1.8% YoY.
points.so_what: The WoW uptick does not recover last year's higher order value, so revenue per order remains below last year's level.

points.what: Cancellation rate was 16.5%, down 0.2pp WoW but up 2.1pp YoY.
points.so_what: The rate remains higher than a year ago even after the weekly dip, a continued drag on order quality.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of Jan 12 was 9.8%, up 0.1pp WoW and 1.1pp YoY.
points.so_what: Returns are trending worse than both the prior week and last year, pointing to weaker order quality.

points.what: New signups rose 12.8% WoW to 273, notably faster than the 1.3% WoW rise in orders.
points.so_what: Signup growth this week outpaced order growth, so it has not yet shown up as a matching increase in orders.

summary.headline: Orders and revenue both finished the week behind target, and the quarter and year remain behind at 94.4% attainment with the pace still below what's required.

points.what: Orders were 99.6% of the weekly target, still behind despite growing 1.3% WoW.
points.so_what: Growth this week was not enough to close the gap to target.

points.what: Revenue was 96.7% of the weekly target despite rising 2.3% WoW.
points.so_what: Revenue growth also fell short of what was needed to meet the target this week.

points.what: QTD and YTD revenue are both at 94.4% of target, with the current 8-week run-rate of $53,042 well below the $75,259 required weekly pace.
points.so_what: At the current pace, the full-year revenue target is not being kept up with.

points.what: EMEA orders grew 20.0% WoW, the top contributor to order growth, while APAC, which holds 39.8% share, fell 9.4% WoW.
points.so_what: Growth this week depended on EMEA offsetting a pullback in APAC, the largest single region by orders.

points.what: Weekly orders were 99.6% of target, a gap of 3 orders, with next week's target rising to 800.
points.so_what: Closing this small gap while facing a higher target next week will need faster growth than this week's pace.

points.what: Weekly revenue was 96.7% of target, a gap of $1,885, and next week's target rises to $61,466.
points.so_what: Revenue growth would need to accelerate meaningfully to meet next week's higher bar.

points.what: QTD and YTD revenue are both at 94.4% of target, a gap of $16,527 so far this year.
points.so_what: The current 8-week run-rate of $53,042 is below the $75,259 needed weekly to reach the full-year target, so the year is not on pace to close this gap.

points.what: Cancellation rate is up 2.1pp YoY to 16.5%.
points.so_what: At $660 of revenue per point of cancellation, this elevated rate versus last year continues to weigh on realized revenue.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of Jan 12 rose to 9.8%, up 1.1pp YoY and 0.1pp WoW.
points.so_what: Returns are increasing versus both the prior week and last year, a risk to order quality this quarter.

points.what: The current 8-week revenue run-rate is $53,042, below the $75,259 weekly pace required to hit the full-year target.
points.so_what: Unless the pace accelerates, the full-year revenue target is at risk of being missed.
